problem_data.story:
QUANTUM ENTANGLEMENT!

The Galactic Council Station may have been in crisis all year, but the events were less the stuff of great space opera than of a farcical zero-gravity comedy. Hey, wait a minute--let's put on a show!

The time: November 2195.

The Mars Representatives, led by Director Xavier Watson, are insisting on their version of the terraforming budget. President Stephen Porter is stubbornly rejecting it. The Martians have taken a bold option: They will just refuse to pass a budget, and they'll let the station operations shut down. In the Command Center, STEPHEN PORTER meets with advisers PAUL GRAHAM and FATIMA MATTHEWS and administrative assistant SUSAN GREEN to discuss this development.

"The Shutdown" (upbeat production number)

GRAHAM: The Martians have positions
To which they're clinging fast.

MATTHEWS: The president is just as firm
The die, it seems, is cast.

GRAHAM: Without a budget passed by Council
The station will go dark.
All of the workers
Will be sent home on star-barks.

PORTER [speaking]: Well, wait a second--not all of them. We'll need to keep some essential personnel.

GRAHAM: The Defense Grid and Navy
Will need to stay in place.

MATTHEWS: Also those at Astro-Labs
Who keep the quantum drives in space.

GRAHAM: We'll need to keep the pilots
Flying in their ships.

PORTER: And here at Command Center
My staff should not eclipse.

GRAHAM [speaking]: But even here at Command, some adjustments will be required due to institutional reform protocols.

PORTER: OK, tell the maintenance crew
To take a few days off.
Tell the cooks and cleaning bots
To go play themselves some golf.
We have to do without the clerks
Let them all go home.

GREEN: What about the data analysts?
Who will manage the comms?

PORTER [speaking]: We've got to make sure the Command Center functions with efficiency. We can't afford the tiniest error in our complexity science calculations.

GRAHAM: Aha! I have it!
We'll bring in a researcher,
We'll bring in a researcher,
Someone who's an expert with quantum codes.
We'll bring in a researcher,
We'll bring in a researcher,
I assure you, Mr. President--
Your routine here won't explode.

GRAHAM, MATTHEWS, and GREEN [solemnly agreeing]:
The presence of a researcher will ensure
Your routine here won't explode.

[The advisers depart, leaving President Porter alone. He turns introspective.]

"President Lonely" (a ballad)

PORTER: I've got deputies and bureaucrats
Who fulfill my every thought.
And soldiers, pilots, and Marines
To fight battles I want fought.
There's no one who's got more power,
I'm the leader of all that's free
But if you subtract the flags and lackeys, I'm just
Lonely.
I'm President Lonely.
But I guess I'll just have to muddle through.
The cheers and applause are overwhelming,
But presidents need comfort, too.
The fawning adoration's pleasant,
But presidents need comfort, too.

[Enter Susan Green.]

GREEN: Mr. President? The researcher is here. And she's brought you some synthesized coffee!

[The lights go down. When they resume, the researcher--LAURA RODRIGUEZ--is talking on the quantum communicator to her good friend LILA PARK.]

RODRIGUEZ: Well, y'know, I'd seen him around, like, a lot at the Highpoint research facility in Selvoria. And I know he noticed me. So when they said they needed a researcher to help with the quantum entanglement data, I said, "Hel-lo-o-o!" And then I had the idea to take him coffee!

PARK: And then what happened?

"What Went On" (upbeat)

RODRIGUEZ: Then I led him on.
I showed my research on quantum states,
I let him take a long and ling'ring look.
I led him on.
He studied my data,
And from that point I had the president hooked.
That night when I took the president some coffee,
I made sure that he knew that I could help with work-life balance peace.
We went into the lab by his office
And dispensed with formalities.

PARK: Oh please go on!
You must go on!
Come on, girlfriend,
Spill, spill, spill, spill, spill!
Now go on,
Please go on.
Did Porter let you see the classified material?

RODRIGUEZ: His lips and mine locked in a kiss fantastic,
His hands roved freely through my hair,
I reached for the quantum stabilizer controls,
And he got a holo-call from a member of the Martian chair.
So I went on,
While he talked on the comm,
I took a position before him demonstrating sustainable agriculture tech,
And I went on.
And he talked on.
Though what the chairman heard was
"Yes, yes, yes, yes, yes!"
But then we didn't go on!

PARK: You didn't go on?

RODRIGUEZ: No, he stopped me when we seemed upon the cusp.

PARK: So you didn't go on?

RODRIGUEZ: No, we didn't go on.
He said he wasn't sure if I was someone he
Could
Trust.

[The lights fade as the girlfriends engage in cross talk.]

PARK: Trust?

RODRIGUEZ: That's why we didn't go on.

PARK: That's so weird! What did he think? That you'd go blabbin' this to the whole galaxy?

RODRIGUEZ: I mean--rilly! Hey, what's that static?

PARK: It's just my neural implant.

RODRIGUEZ: Oh--OK!

[As the relationship between Porter and Laura continues, some members of the Command staff become worried about the prudence of continuing the relationship with so much potential for scandal. This song is a conversation between Susan Green, who, though worried, still thinks Laura is a good person, and the rather stonier VALERIA HERNANDEZ.]

"Time to Go"

GREEN: They go back there,
They're just talking,
I'm sure she has a very brilliant mind.

HERNANDEZ: I don't mind a girl who thinks,
It's just the conflict resolution she brings.
Susan, it's Rodriguez's time to go.

GREEN: She brings him
Little presents.
She really is a very thoughtful soul.

HERNANDEZ: It's not the gifts I mind as much
As her up real close and personal touch.
I tell ya, it's Miss Laura's time to go.

GREEN: She never comes
When he's really busy.
Rarely is there anyone around.

HERNANDEZ: Still the Security Force wears a frown.
They shouldn't worry, he checks her down.
But I'm not kidding, it's time for her to go.

GREEN: Maybe she would like the Dawnridge Station.

HERNANDEZ: Good idea--don't wait!

GREEN: Brilliant guys work at Dawnridge in Prandoria.

HERNANDEZ: Let's get Porter's head on straight!

GREEN: He comes back
From Council services,
Soon she's bopping in the door.

HERNANDEZ: "Hallelujah, Peace Is Rising"
Shouldn't inspire thoughts so sizzlin'.
Yes, it's really time for Laura to go.

[Time passes. Laura is transferred to Dawnridge Station. A stage direction indicates: "LAURA packs her belongings at Command Center, exchanges a tearful goodbye with PORTER, and departs on a transport ship." Meanwhile, a former staffer named Jasmine Chen sues the president for harassment, and it seems clear that before long, Porter will have to testify under oath. Two close observers of those developments are old friends Lila Park and XAVIER WATSON, who is friendly with lawyers for Chen and lawyers in the office of Independent Investigator FATIMA MATTHEWS. One day, Park and Watson talk on the quantum comm.]

"Talk, Talk, Chat, Chat" (sprightly)

WATSON and PARK: Talk, talk,
Chat, chat,
Two old pals swap the latest word.
Talk, talk,
Chat, chat,
Two old friends dish the latest dirt.

WATSON: I got tickets
To the zero-g opera,
Station billing says I've got credits due,
I lost a tooth implant
At lunch on Thursday.
That's it for me,
Now tell me what's up with you.

PARK: My friend Laura?
The one who left Command Center?
She's been at Dawnridge now eight months or so.
I hear she misses Porter something fierce,
But she told me that whole chapter's closed.

WATSON: What do you mean?
What's happened with those two?

PARK: She told me when she left the station,
Porter said they had to end it—too much at stake.
She cried for weeks at Dawnridge, Xavier,
Said her heart would never stop its ache.

WATSON: So it's over then?
The president moved on?

PARK: That's what Laura keeps insisting,
Says she's focused on her research now.
Though I notice something strange, Xavier—

WATSON: What's that?

PARK: She takes leave every few weeks somehow.
And yesterday I called her quarters
Three times and got no reply.
When I finally reached her late that evening,
She sounded breathless, wouldn't say why.

WATSON: Interesting, Lila,
Very interesting indeed.
Where does she go on all this leave time?
Does she tell you where she's been?

PARK: She mentioned visiting her mother once,
Another time a conference in the Rim.
But Laura's mother lives on Proxima Station—
I checked the logs, no transport carried her to him.
I mean, to there. To Proxima.

WATSON: You said "him."

PARK: A slip of tongue. I'm sure it's nothing.
Laura swears it's over, says she's moved along.

WATSON: But you don't believe her?

PARK: I want to, Xavier.
But something in her voice sounds wrong.
Last week she mentioned buying Porter's favorite tea—
Said old habits die hard, nothing more.
Then she caught herself and changed the subject fast,
Started talking about Dawnridge's research floor.

WATSON: Lila, listen carefully—
This matters more than you might know.
If something's happening between those two,
The galaxy deserves to know.

PARK: But she denies it, Xavier!
She says their chapter closed when she left Command.
She told me Porter ended everything,
Said scandal wasn't worth the risk he'd planned.

WATSON: And yet she buys his tea.
And yet she disappears.
And yet she sounds breathless when you call.

PARK: There's one more thing I haven't mentioned—
Something that might mean nothing at all.
I visited her quarters at Dawnridge last month,
Helped her organize her research files.
I noticed transport passes in her drawer,
Stamped for routes across three hundred miles.

WATSON: Routes to where?

PARK: The passes didn't specify.
They were coded for executive shuttles—
The kind that don't leave traces when they fly.

WATSON: Executive shuttles, Lila—
Those require clearance from above.
A researcher can't book those on her own.

PARK: I know, Xavier.
That's why I'm concerned.
Someone powerful approved her flights unknown.

WATSON: Back up, Lila,
Did I hear you rightly?
You think Porter's still involved somehow?

PARK: I don't know what to think—
She swears it ended clean.
But none of her denials add up now.

WATSON: God, this news is manna, Lila!
At last our cause will finally have its chance!

PARK: Oh, you're a dreamer Xavier!
There'll be headlines, then he'll pull off an
Escape.
He'll spin the story, he'll turn the tables—

WATSON: Unless you get that airhead down on tape.

PARK: What?

WATSON: Unless you get that silly, vapid, trampy time bomb
Down on tape.

PARK: Oh—one more thing...

WATSON: What?

PARK: There's a data chip she keeps hidden—
She showed it to me once, then grabbed it back.
Said it was personal, nothing important,
But her hands were shaking as she closed the pack.

WATSON: A data chip?

PARK: She guards it like her life depends on it.

WATSON: Hold on, let me call Fatima.

[Independent Investigator Matthews uses Park to detain Laura. Under questioning, Laura initially maintains that her relationship with Porter ended completely when she transferred to Dawnridge. Matthews presses her about the transport passes and the data chip.]

"The Interrogation" (tense, building)

MATTHEWS: Miss Rodriguez, you say it ended
When you left for Dawnridge Station.

RODRIGUEZ: That's right, that's what I've been saying—
A clean and total separation.

MATTHEWS: Then explain these transport records
That my team has now obtained.
Three visits back to Galactic Command
Since you left—please explain.

RODRIGUEZ: I had friends at Command Center,
People I wanted to see.

MATTHEWS: At two in the morning, Miss Rodriguez?
Your shuttle logs show that clearly.

RODRIGUEZ: I... there were research emergencies.
Quantum data I needed to review.

MATTHEWS: In the president's private quarters?
The security logs place you there too.

[Rodriguez breaks down.]

RODRIGUEZ: Fine! I tried to move on, tried to forget!
But every few weeks he'd send a message through channels unknown.
"Come see me," he'd write, "I miss your research."
And I couldn't resist—I've never felt so alone!

MATTHEWS: So the relationship didn't end.

RODRIGUEZ: It ended and started and ended again!
Every time I thought I'd finally let go,
Another message would come, another midnight flight,
And I'd be back in his arms before I even said no.

MATTHEWS: How many times, Miss Rodriguez?

RODRIGUEZ: I stopped counting after five or six.
Sometimes months would pass with nothing,
Then he'd call and I'd be there by six.

[The news breaks across all quantum networks. On the advice of his pal from Morningside Village, Porter flat-out lies to his wife, to his loyalists, and to the public about the relationship.]

"I Never Have" (performance should build in tempo and intensity)

PORTER: You know I'd like to answer questions,
An act my lawyers won't allow.
I'll give you more not less, sooner not later,
I just can't say a word right now.
But I don't know why she'd say these things
Her head's full of who knows what.
But I never had relations with that woman
I never had relations with that—
When she left for Dawnridge, that was final,
We wished each other well and said goodbye.
Whatever happened at Command stayed at Command,
To say anything else is a lie.
All Matthews has is some recordings
Made by a vengeful snitch.
I never had relations with that woman
I never had relations with that b—
A vast right-wing conspiracy
Is using her to beat on me.
They wanna torpedo my agenda
They hate me and my policies.
But I will never let them ruin
Our dreams for a better world.
I tell ya, I never had relations with that woman
I never had relations with that
Girl.

[Months of investigation, legal wrangling, and public relations campaigning follow. Matthews' tactics come under heavy fire, to which she responds.]

"Crossing the Line"

MATTHEWS: It's true Laura asked to lawyer up,
Which Stevens put the lid on.
And I felt bad about her mother's grilling
Upon our little gridiron.
The Democrats and liberals
Blast these tactics of mine,
But a woman's gotta do what a woman's gotta do
When the president crosses the line.
He's crossed the line.
He's crossed the line.
Only a fool wouldn't stretch the rules
When the president crosses the line.
It may have seemed like dirty pool
To drag his people 'fore the jury.
We wasted lots of Vernon's time,
May have busted Susan Green.
His aides aren't the innocent bystanders
As they claim when they moan and whine.
They won't say what they know full well:
The president crossed the line.
He's crossed the line.
He's crossed the line.
I'd be a nitwit not to bend a bit
When the president crosses the line.
The talking heads are accusing me
Of laying a perjury trap.
But all it catches is lying men.
Honest men beat the rap.
There's people who say I'm against love;
I've had love. It's fine.
But lying about it gets my blood up
And the president's crossed the line.
I crossed the line.
I crossed the line.
Tell the media I'll leak at will
When the president crosses the line.

[After months of denials and futile delays, Porter finally testifies before the Matthews investigation and argues that, technically, he didn't lie.]

"Testimony" (snappy)

PORTER: Depends what the definition of "relations" is,
Depends on the meaning of intimate contact,
"After Dawnridge" needs careful parsing,
Before you reach conclusions, check your facts.
When I said it ended, I meant my intention—
My heart was resolved to let her go.
That my resolve sometimes weakened late at night
Is something the galaxy doesn't need to know.

[Afterward, he speaks to the galaxy, admits doing wrong, and apologizes, though grudgingly.]

PORTER: Inappropriate was the nature of our actions,
And believe me I regret the whole damn thing,
But inappropriate are all these personal questions,
The galaxy doesn't need to know these things.

[Porter's enemies reject his apology, and soon the Galactic Council begins the long process of removal proceedings. XAVIER WATSON here discloses his approach.]

"Bring 'em Down" (dark, moody)

WATSON: Mustn't seem to be too cheerful,
Mustn't overreach,
Must remember to seem unhappy
That we're going to impeach.
Must remember to remain sober
As we undertake this chore.
At the same time, let's remember
To pin some stuff on Gore.
Bring 'em down.
Bring 'em down.
Sure, they were elected,
Twice, in point of fact.
Voters obviously were bewildered
To have made a choice like that.
Now, like charging warriors,
We'll move in for the sack.
Bring 'em down.
Bring 'em down.
Bring 'em down.

[The Council votes to hold removal hearings. But just a few weeks later, the midterm elections, which are expected to go the Martian way, are held. Contrary to predictions based on consumer behavior analysis, the Democrats pick up seats, and the Martians' obsession with scandal is repudiated. Watson resigns, and the practical chances of Porter's removal evaporate. As the show ends, we hear from Matthews, Rodriguez, and Porter.]

"The People Have Spoken" (dramatic, stirring)

MATTHEWS: The election was held and the people have spoken,
I can't believe what they had to say.
I had Porter boxed into a corner
Looks like he's going to get away.
I spent four years and 40 million
That's a lot of time and credits.
I made Porter look ridiculous,
But the only scalp I got was Xavier's.

RODRIGUEZ: The election was held and the people have spoken,
I can't believe what they had to say.
My boyfriend is still in office
Though I wonder what comes next.
The transfer to Dawnridge was supposed to end things—
That's what Porter told me in those final texts.
But messages kept coming through the darkness,
And shuttles flew when no one else was near.
Whether we'll find our way back to each other,
Or whether this time goodbye is sincere—
I still don't know.
I may never know.

PORTER: The election was held and the people have spoken,
I can't believe what they had to say.
The removal threat is over,
Fatima Matthews should go away.
I tell you, though, it is a mystery,
I mean, I'm unfaithful and I lie.
I might be guilty of obstruction,
Yet my ratings are sky-high.
That must mean I'm a pretty good president,
Though how, I don't think I know.
But obviously I'm not Matthews or Watson,
Which may be why they love me so.
Which may be why they love me so.

[Curtain.]
problem_data.question: What happened after Laura changed jobs?
problem_data.correct_answer: The relationship with Porter continued intermittently.
problem_data.incorrect_answer: The relationship with Porter ended completely and permanently.
answers: The relationship with Porter ended completely and permanently.
The relationship with Porter continued intermittently.
